name: rsi_connors_pullback_v41
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, institutional TWAP/VWAP algorithms working large directional orders create persistent intraday trends over 20-45 minute windows. Within these trends, reactive retail stops and short-term momentum algos trigger brief 10-30 second counter-trend micro-pullbacks visible as extremely low RSI(6) readings (30-second RSI). The institutional order that created the trend has not been fully filled — when the micro-counter-move exhausts at RSI < 25, the underlying TWAP buy side resumes and NIFTY snaps back in the trend direction within 15-60 seconds. The edge is that RSI(6) detects the last sellers/buyers capitulating before the institutional engine resumes.

indicators.name: sma_360
indicators.purpose: 30-minute intraday trend filter. The original used SMA(200) on 15-min bars = 50 hours of data as a multi-day macro trend filter. At 5s bars, the relevant 'longer-term' context is the intraday trend, not multi-day — NIFTY options expire daily and intraday trend is what drives directional flow. 30 min = 360 bars captures a full TWAP/VWAP cycle that institutional algorithms typically run, without reaching back to prior session data. NOT a 12x blind scale (which would give SMA(2400) = 3.3 hours — too slow for 5s trading).

indicators.name: rsi_6
indicators.purpose: 30-second RSI exhaustion trigger. Original uses RSI(2) at 15-min = measures exhaustion over 2 bars × 15 min = 30 minutes. We want to match this 'exhaustion time window' proportionally to our hold time: original holds ~200 min, we hold ~30s, ratio ~6x. So 30 min / 6 = 5 min... but at 5s bars RSI(60) = 5 min is too smooth to catch micro-pullbacks. The key insight from Connors RSI(2) is that the RSI period must be SHORT enough to reach extreme levels (< 25 or > 75) on very brief counter-moves. RSI(6) = 30s is the minimum period that yields stable extremes without pure tick noise — RSI(2) at 5s (10s window) would oscillate 0-100 on nearly every bar.

conditions: rsi_6 < 25 (30-second RSI shows extreme oversold — micro-pullback exhausted)
vix < vix_max (avoid high-volatility regimes where mean reversion fails)
rsi_6 > 75 (30-second RSI shows extreme overbought — micro-bounce exhausted)

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option points = ~6 spot points of adverse move. If the micro-pullback continues past 6 spot points against trend direction after the RSI signal, the institutional TWAP order has likely paused or reversed — the thesis is invalidated. NIFTY 30-second ATM option moves of 2-5 pts; a 3 pt stop gives room for the signal bar's noise without excessive losses.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option points = ~10 spot points of favorable move. NIFTY micro-pullback restorations (RSI(6) exhaustion to trend resumption) typically cover 8-15 spot points in the first 30-60 seconds, translating to 4-7 option points at ATM delta ~0.5. Target of 5 pts captures the lower-median of this distribution, yielding 1:1.67 R:R at stop=3.

filters.vix_filter: vix < 20 (high VIX sessions see erratic micro-moves that break RSI mean-reversion thesis)
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST — skip first 15 minutes for trend to establish via SMA(360) warmup
filters.volume_filter: none (NIFTY index volume is noisy at 5s; rely on price action)
filters.trend_filter: SMA(360) direction check embedded in entry conditions
filters.spread_filter: none (limit orders at candle close, no spread cost)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — if institutional TWAP patterns shift or SEBI changes algo regulations, intraday trend persistence changes

adaptation_notes: Three key changes from original: (1) Trend filter compressed from SMA(200) at 15-min (50-hour multi-day trend) to SMA(360) at 5s (30-min intraday trend) — NIFTY options are daily instruments so intraday trend is the relevant context, not multi-day. (2) RSI period: kept the concept of 'very fast RSI' but used RSI(6) instead of RSI(2) — at 5s bars, RSI(2) is pure noise (10s window); RSI(6) = 30s is the minimum period yielding meaningful exhaustion readings. (3) Short entry threshold adapted from RSI(2) > 30 (original, which seems like a bug — likely meant > 70 for Connors symmetry) to RSI(6) > 75, making the short symmetric to the long. Hold time compressed from 150-450 min to 15-60s — we trade the instantaneous micro-bounce, not the multi-hour recovery.
weaknesses: RSI(6) generates many false signals in choppy NIFTY sessions with no intraday trend (common on 2-3 days per week)
SMA(360) is a lagging trend filter — in fast trend reversals, can be on wrong side for 10-15 minutes
Micro-pullbacks sometimes deepen into full trend reversals; 3pt stop may get hit repeatedly in whipsaw conditions
Low trade count per day (3-8) limits statistical significance in short backtests
